title: Two American Economists Win the Nobel Prize in Economics
summary:
Two American-born economists, Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford, have won this year's Nobel memorial prize in economics. The winners were announced Monday in Stockholm, Sweden, by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.

Economics is the study of how people, businesses and governments make choices about money, jobs and goods. Hall and Woodford were honored for creating models that help governments and central banks deal with economic shocks. A central bank is a country's main bank, which helps manage money and interest rates. Shocks are sudden changes, such as an energy crisis or a quick change in how much families spend.

"The laureates have helped us smooth out the economy's peaks and troughs," the academy said. In other words, their work helps keep the economy from swinging too far up or down.

For decades, many governments followed the ideas of a British economist named John Maynard Keynes. When the economy slowed, governments lowered taxes and spent more money to help growth start again. But in the 1970s, many countries faced high prices and high unemployment at the same time. That showed the old ideas were too simple.

Working separately, Hall and Woodford built better models that consider how people and businesses actually decide whether to spend or invest. John Hassler, who leads the prize committee, said their work gave a stable foundation for models now used by central banks and governments around the world.

Woodford spoke to the committee by phone from New York. "It's a tremendous honour, it's a surprise," he said.

The economics prize was created in 1968 by Sweden's central bank in memory of Alfred Nobel. It is presented with the other Nobel Prizes on Dec. 10.
why_it_matters: When energy crises or sudden spending changes hit, better economic models help governments and central banks protect jobs and keep prices steadier for families.

background_read: The Nobel Prizes are among the world's best-known awards, created in memory of Alfred Nobel to honor major achievements in science, literature and peace.
The economics prize was added later by Sweden's central bank and is awarded alongside the other Nobel Prizes.
Economists build models, which are simplified descriptions of how an economy works, to predict what might happen when something suddenly changes.
Governments and central banks use these predictions when deciding how to respond to problems like rising prices or falling spending.
